role_place: Anglican dean of Norwich; English apologist; book on the life of Mahomet written for English deists.
why_relevant: Explicit English statement of Aisha's age at marriage and consummation, with an explanation of it by the custom of hot countries, and a remark that Mahomet's Imposture served his lust.
fame: Known mainly for his Old and New Testament connection (1716-18) and for the Life of Mahomet, a standard early-modern English life of the Prophet.

role_place: Professor of Oriental languages at Oxford; compiled La Vie de Mahomet (1732) from Abulfeda, Arabic traditions and Arab authors.
why_relevant: Gives Aisha's age as seven at the marriage and nine at consummation in a neutral narrative, with an explicit list of the Prophet's wives.
fame: Known as an Arabist and editor of Abulfeda's life of Muhammad (Latin, 1723) and the French Vie de Mahomet (1732).

role_place: Dutch orientalist at Utrecht; De religione Mohammedica libri duo (1705).
why_relevant: Lists Muhammad's wives and names Aisha ('Aifcha') as the only virgin among them, from 'reliable records', with no age given.
fame: Respected Dutch Arabist and Islamicist; De religione Mohammedica was a standard early-modern Latin account of Islam.

role_place: French aristocratic historian; La vie de Mahomed (1730, posthumous), a favourable life of the Prophet.
why_relevant: Favourable to Muhammad, yet describes Aisha as 'fort jeune' at the marriage and argues she was probably a virgin; the youngest wife, given to coquetry, which he attributes to her youth.
fame: Known as a writer on the history of the Franks; his Vie de Mahomed was a sympathetic 18th-century life of the Prophet, published in English in 1731.
community: Catholic (French aristocrat), sympathetic to Islam in this work
